edges.mechanism: Pyridoxine (10-25 mg) accelerates peripheral aromatic amino acid decarboxylation of levodopa, reversing its effect; carbidopa blocks this.
edges.evidence: FDA label (Sinemet clinical pharmacology); classic metabolic studies and reviews

edges.mechanism: Carbidopa binds PLP; high carbidopa exposure (incl. foslevodopa/foscarbidopa infusion) associated with low B6 biomarkers and neuropathy. B6 supplementation does not reduce carbidopa-levodopa efficacy.
edges.evidence: Label statement; scoping review (36 reports) with no established threshold; case series; low certainty

edges.mechanism: High-dose pyridoxine reported to lower serum phenytoin; phenytoin and other anti-seizure drugs can lower plasma PLP.
edges.evidence: Case-level report (Lancet letter); GeneReviews advice; low certainty

edges.mechanism: High-dose pyridoxine reported to lower serum phenobarbitone; phenobarbital can lower plasma PLP.
edges.evidence: Case-level report; GeneReviews advice; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Isoniazid antagonises PLP and causes polyneuropathy; pyridoxine co-administration prevents it, especially in high-risk groups such as HIV co-infection.
edges.evidence: Clinical studies since 1956 and systematic review; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Theophylline noncompetitively inhibits pyridoxal kinase, lowering plasma and erythrocyte PLP; 10 mg/d pyridoxine normalizes status.
edges.evidence: Placebo-controlled human studies and crystallography

edges.mechanism: Hydrazine drug that depletes B6 and can cause pyridoxine-deficiency neuropathy.
edges.evidence: Case report (NEJM 1965); review

edges.mechanism: Penicillamine inactivates PLP, interrupting the tryptophan-niacin pathway in Wilson disease.
edges.evidence: Human and animal studies; review

edges.mechanism: Estrogen-progestin contraceptives can lower PLP in a subset of users; 10 mg/d pyridoxine restores PLP and normalizes metabolite profiles.
edges.evidence: RCT of 7 low-dose OCs (transient PLP fall) and supplementation study (n=10); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Fixed-dose doxylamine 10 mg + pyridoxine 10 mg delayed-release (Diclegis) for nausea and vomiting of pregnancy; benefit is modest (PUQE about -0.7 to -1.0).
edges.evidence: FDA label; RCTs and reanalysis; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Riboflavin (as FMN) is the cofactor of PNPO, which forms PLP; poor riboflavin status lowers plasma PLP.
edges.evidence: Observational studies (n=407; n=5612) and review

edges.mechanism: Folate plus B6/B12 lowers homocysteine; combinations reduced stroke modestly but not MI or mortality. Folic acid plus B12 (not B6) linked to cancer increase in Norway.
edges.evidence: Cochrane MA of 15 RCTs; HOPE-2; NORVIT/WENBIT pooled

edges.mechanism: Combined high B6 and B12 intake associated with higher hip-fracture risk; individual B6 (>20 mg/d) and B12 supplements associated with lung cancer in men; NORVIT combined arm showed harm trend.
edges.evidence: Large cohorts (NHS n=75,864; VITAL n=77,118) and RCT; very low to low certainty

edges.mechanism: Stacking B-complex/multivitamin products with B6 supplements raises cumulative intake; neuropathy reported even at 6 mg/d and with B-complex use.
edges.evidence: Pharmacovigilance (Lareb), case reports, TGA review

edges.mechanism: Many magnesium products contain B6 (often 30 mg); TGA advises checking magnesium and zinc products for hidden B6. Mg+B6 not superior to Mg alone for stress overall.
edges.evidence: Regulator advice; RCT (n=264)

edges.mechanism: Zinc combination products can contain undeclared-by-common-name B6, adding to cumulative exposure.
edges.evidence: Regulator advice (TGA)

edges.mechanism: In cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency, pyridoxine responders are treated with B6 while non/partial responders need betaine plus low-methionine diet.
edges.evidence: Guideline and E-HOD registry

edges.mechanism: Excess pyridoxine causes sensory axonal neuropathy, plausibly via PDXK inhibition; cases at <50 mg/d; EFSA UL 12 mg/d.
edges.evidence: Case series, pharmacovigilance (90 and 224 reports), SR, regulatory opinion

edges.mechanism: Low TNSALP activity raises plasma PLP (diagnostic marker); supplements confound PLP and are unnecessary for raised levels.
edges.evidence: Cohort and biochemical studies; reviews

edges.mechanism: Supplements raise plasma B6 far above reference (Lareb mean 907 nmol/L vs 51-183 reference); PLP also lowered by inflammation, low albumin and high ALP independently of intake.
edges.evidence: Pharmacovigilance and biomarker reviews

edges.mechanism: ALPL rs4654748 is the main GWAS locus for serum B6; pathogenic ALPL variants cause hypophosphatasia with high PLP.
edges.evidence: GWAS (n~2900 + replication); cohort

edges.mechanism: Most patients need PLP rather than pyridoxine; high-dose PLP linked to liver toxicity (20%) and hepatocellular carcinoma cases.
edges.evidence: SR of 49 patients; GeneReviews; case reports
